subject: ASPEST kickoff - abstain smartly, label smartly
body:
Team,

Kicking off the Active Selective Prediction track. The deployment story we keep failing to tell: when a customer's data shifts, their model should (a) know when to abstain and route to a human, and (b) spend the resulting human-labeling budget on the points that fix it fastest. ASPEST, from our open-source release, does both at once - that's the bridge between active learning and selective prediction, and no one else in our stack has it.

The repo ships six shift benchmarks - mnist->svhn, cifar10->cinic10, fmow, amazon_review, domainnet, and otto - four available via TensorFlow Datasets and the rest downloaded manually, with a build_datasets.sh script to standardize everything.

Milestones: benchmark suite built and repro complete in May; integration design with the human-review routing layer by June 19; pilot-ready eval report by July 24, ahead of an LRB slot in early August.

Alina - staffing and compute please. May is the make-or-break month.

Dmitri
